paper.purpose: The page ground, set on body. Warm at hue 85 so no card ever reads clinical against it.

surface.purpose: Pure white. Every card, table, dialog, and chip sits on it — the only achromatic token in the palette.

surface-sunken.purpose: The resting fill of a filter chip and the pressed state of a dialog button. One step below the page.

surface-hover.purpose: Dropdown items, dialog buttons, and unselected chips on hover. Half a step, never a colour change.

surface-subtle.purpose: Shares paper exactly. Fills table cells, form fields, and dropdown menus so a field reads as recessed into the card.

surface-band.purpose: An opaque warm band for odd table rows. Not a translucent ink overlay — that is why banding no longer reads blue.

hairline.purpose: The default 1px separation between surfaces. Structure comes from this, not from shadow.

hairline-strong.purpose: Table row rules, modal header and footer divisions, and the chip separator. Also aliased as control-border.

ink.purpose: Body text and every figure. Warm at hue 60 at 16.48:1 on surface; nothing on screen is neutral black.

ink-soft.purpose: Every piece of small text — labels, captions, the build hash, table meta. 6.02:1, which is what keeps small text legal.

ink-faint.purpose: Not body text. 3.65:1 clears non-text and AA large only: axis ticks, disabled glyphs, decorative rules.

brass.purpose: The one accent. Navigation state, focus ring, primary action, active filter chip. Nothing else may claim it.

brass-deep.purpose: Brass as text on a brass wash, the primary gradient end stop, and every table column header.

brass-wash.purpose: The active filter chip fill and every brass-tinted hover. Fifteen declarations and the busiest wash in the system.

gain.purpose: Positive signed monetary movement. Locked to L = 0.520 against loss.

gain-deep.purpose: Gain one step down, for gradient end stops and text on a gain wash.

gain-wash.purpose: Positive badge fills and the upward half of the price-flash animation.

loss.purpose: Negative signed monetary movement, at the same lightness as gain so an equal loss cannot look louder.

loss-deep.purpose: Loss one step down: gradient end stops, danger alert text, destructive hover fills.

loss-wash.purpose: Negative badge fills, the danger alert ground, and the downward half of the price flash.

loss-wash-deep.purpose: A border colour only — the danger alert edge and destructive-button hovers. Never a fill.

notice.purpose: Informational signal, held at the gain/loss lightness so it cannot outrank either.

series-5.purpose: The fifth quantitative hue. Declared and contrast-gated; no component consumes it yet.

series-6.purpose: The sixth quantitative hue, lifted to 0.58 to clear 3:1 at its lower chroma.

display.purpose: h1 only, at clamp(2.5rem, 1.6rem + 3.6vw, 3.5rem) / 550 / -0.01em. The tracking matches the -0.48px Lightyear sets on its own 48px price figure.

title.purpose: h2 and every stat-card value, at clamp(1.5rem, 1.3rem + 0.9vw, 1.875rem) / 550. A number large enough to be the point of its card is set at 550, not 400.

heading.purpose: h3 and card headers at clamp(1.125rem, 1.05rem + 0.35vw, 1.25rem) / 550. Not 600 — in a document made of tables a 600 heading over a 600 figure flattens the hierarchy it was meant to create.

control.purpose: The resting size of an interactive control at 1rem: .btn, .form-control, .form-select, .input-group-text, .dropdown-menu. One step above body, inherited from the pre-Tailwind control layer.

body.purpose: Prose, form values, dialog text, and h6 at 0.9375rem / 400. The least-used role in a system made of tables.

control-sm.purpose: The -sm control variant, plus .toast and .dialog-btn, at 0.875rem.

dense.purpose: Table meta and compacted mobile values at 0.8125rem.

label.purpose: Uppercase, weight 600, 0.05em tracking. The system most recognizable typographic gesture: brass-deep at 0.75rem on table headers, gray-700 at 0.8125rem on mobile card fields. Ten further variants exist across five specs and are debt, not precedent.

numerals.purpose: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set once on body and inherits everywhere. Every right-aligned money column depends on it, and so does the price-flash animation not making digits jitter.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Cards, card shells, and the desktop table wrapper. Tinted from ink, never from neutral black — a warm surface casting a cool shadow is the tell that a palette was retoned but its elevation was not.

shadows.name: shadow-control
shadows.purpose: Buttons and ghost controls. Inverted to inset on press so the button reads as depressed rather than moved.

shadows.name: shadow-lifted
shadows.purpose: The dropdown menu, mobile card hover, and the ETF holding logo lift. The strongest shadow in routine use.

shadows.name: shadow-nav
shadows.purpose: The sticky navbar at 992px and up. A hairline rendered as a shadow, not an elevation.

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Toasts and the native select picker. The only shadow allowed to be seen from across the room, because a toast has to arrive.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state transition in the system. Declared in @theme static; the durations below are declared in a :root block at the head of base.css because Tailwind has no namespace for them.

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, and colour transitions on buttons, form fields, dropdown items, and mobile cards. Also the native select picker open and close.

motion.name: transition-base
motion.purpose: The add-new button and its + glyph.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: The nav indicator scaleX, the nav link colour, and the route fade-slide across 20px of translateY.

motion.name: transition-chip
motion.purpose: Filter chips, time-range chips, and dialog buttons only, on plain ease rather than the standard curve. A faster tier that makes filtering feel immediate.

motion.name: value-flash
motion.purpose: The price-change pulse: transparent to gain-wash or loss-wash and back. Exempt from prefers-reduced-motion by an explicit 3s !important override, because the flash is information rather than decoration.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: Opacity oscillation from 0.6 to 0.8 across loading placeholders.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: Button, page, and bordered spinners. Kept running under prefers-reduced-motion so a working control still reads as working.

motion.name: chip-press
motion.purpose: The only transform in the chip vocabulary. Buttons translateY(1px) instead; a chip is pressed, a button is pushed.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: The signature switch: data tables become label/value card stacks below this, and every .btn takes a 44px min-height. --container-app also drops to 100%.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: Navigation becomes sticky and picks up shadow-nav; .modal-lg widens to 800px.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.note: Declared token. No media query hangs off it — the fluid clamp() ramp is what stops growing near here.

breakpoints.name: 2xl
breakpoints.note: Declared token; no layout change hangs off it.

breakpoints.name: ad-hoc-389
breakpoints.note: Small-phone compaction tier for mobile card padding and value size.

breakpoints.name: ad-hoc-666
breakpoints.note: Data table collapses to data-label prefixed blocks.

breakpoints.name: ad-hoc-844
breakpoints.note: Tablet band: icon-plus-label ghost buttons tighten to 0.375rem 0.5rem so action rows do not wrap.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action on a screen. The 135deg brass gradient reverses on hover rather than lightening, so the control darkens into the press instead of glowing. Still authored against the legacy signal-indigo alias, which holds the brass value.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; color: #ffffff; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #8d621f 0%, #784e00 100%); border: 1px solid #d2cfc8; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0.24 0.012 60 / 0.04); cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #784e00 0%, #8d621f 100%); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8d621f; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The default action in a table row or toolbar. Rests as a hairline outline over a 2% ink film and only becomes brass on hover, so a row of six actions reads as one quiet group until it is approached.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; color: #69625b; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.02); border: 1px solid #d2cfc8; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0.24 0.012 60 / 0.04); cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #784e00; background-color: #f8eee2; } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8d621f; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Selected-one-of-many, and the system busiest control: platform filters, ETF dimension tabs, and the summary chart time range all use this exact rule. Resting is a sunken warm fill with a transparent border, so selecting a chip adds an edge rather than moving the text. Active is brass-wash with a brass border and an inset ring of the same wash, which thickens the edge without a second colour.
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.3rem; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; color: #69625b; background: #f6f3ed; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.3125rem 0.6875rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 120ms ease; } .ds-chip:hover { color: #241e1a; background: #f9f6f2; border-color: #d2cfc8; } .ds-chip:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-chip.is-active { color: #784e00; background: #f8eee2; border-color: #8d621f; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #f8eee2; } .ds-chip.is-active:hover { border-color: #784e00; }

components.name: Dialog Button
components.description: The action row of a dialog, on the 120ms chip tier rather than the 150ms control tier. Its primary variant fills with ink-soft rather than brass — inside a dialog the accent is already spent on the focus ring, and a brass confirm beside a brass ring reads as two primaries.
components.css: .ds-dialog-actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-dialog-btn { font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; color: #69625b; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2dfda; border-radius: 0.25rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 120ms ease; } .ds-dialog-btn:hover { color: #69625b; background: #f9f6f2; border-color: #d2cfc8; } .ds-dialog-btn:active { background: #f6f3ed; transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-dialog-btn.is-primary { color: #ffffff; background: #69625b; border-color: #69625b; } .ds-dialog-btn.is-primary:hover { background: #241e1a; border-color: #241e1a; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Fields are filled with surface-subtle rather than surface, so a field reads as recessed into the card it sits on rather than raised off it. Focus carries both a brass border and the 2px brass ring at 2px offset; the doubled treatment is deliberate on a form where a mistyped figure is a wrong number.
components.css: .ds-form-label { display: inline-block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-input { display: block; width: 100%; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.5; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #241e1a; background-color: #fcfaf6; border: 1px solid #d2cfc8; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; appearance: none; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #69625b; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #8d621f; outline: 2px solid #8d621f; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-input.is-invalid { border-color: #b33834; }

components.name: Native Select Picker
components.description: A real <select> styled through appearance: base-select and ::picker(select), behind an @supports guard that falls back to the SVG chevron. Options are brass-wash on hover and on :checked, the checkmark is brass, and the picker fades and translates 0.25rem over 150ms with display and overlay transitioned allow-discrete plus a @starting-style entry. Nothing here is a custom listbox: the top layer, the keyboard model, and scroll containment are the platform.
components.css: .ds-select { display: block; width: 100%; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; color: #241e1a; background-color: #fcfaf6; border: 1px solid #d2cfc8; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 0.375rem 2.25rem 0.375rem 0.75rem; } @supports (appearance: base-select) { .ds-select, .ds-select::picker(select) { appearance: base-select; } .ds-select::picker-icon { display: none; } .ds-select::picker(select) { padding: 0.25rem; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #d2cfc8; border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 0.5rem 1.5rem oklch(0.24 0.012 60 / 0.14); opacity: 1; translate: 0 0; transition: opacity 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), translate 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), display 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) allow-discrete, overlay 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) allow-discrete; } .ds-select:not(:open)::picker(select) { opacity: 0; translate: 0 -0.25rem; } @starting-style { .ds-select:open::picker(select) { opacity: 0; translate: 0 -0.25rem; } } .ds-select option { padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; color: #241e1a; } .ds-select option:hover, .ds-select option:focus { background: #f8eee2; color: #784e00; } .ds-select option:checked { background: #f8eee2; color: #784e00; font-weight: 550; } .ds-select option::checkmark { color: #8d621f; } }

components.name: Data Table
components.description: The desktop primitive the whole system is built around. Column headers carry the label gesture in brass-deep — the one place the accent appears as text — and cells are filled with surface-subtle so the table body recedes below its own header. There is no background fill on thead th: it was removed because it collided with the brass-wash filter chips sitting directly above the table.
components.css: .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #241e1a; background-color: #ffffff; } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { padding: 1rem 0.75rem; vertical-align: middle; background-color: #fcfaf6; border-bottom: 1px solid #d2cfc8; } .ds-table thead th { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; text-align: left; color: #784e00; } .ds-table tbody tr.band > * { background-color: #f6f3ed; } .ds-table .num { text-align: right; }

components.name: Mobile Data Card
components.description: What every table becomes below 768px — the signature responsive move. Each row turns into label/value pairs, the label taking the gesture one size up at 0.8125rem because it stands beside its value rather than at the head of an aligned column. Shipping a new data column means shipping both renderings.
components.css: .ds-mobile-card { font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; padding: 1.25rem 0.75rem; margin-bottom: 0.875rem; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #eae7e2; border-radius: 0.75rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.03); transition: all 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-mobile-card:hover { border-color: #e2dfda; } .ds-mc-item { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.875rem 0; } .ds-mc-item:nth-child(2) { padding-bottom: 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #f9f6f2; } .ds-mc-label { flex: 0 0 auto; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #4e4640; } .ds-mc-value { flex: 1; margin-left: auto; font-weight: 600; text-align: right; word-break: break-word; }

components.name: Stat Card
components.description: The extracted shared primitive behind every headline figure. The label takes the gesture at weight 500 rather than 600, and the value is set at title size and weight 550 — a number large enough to be the point of its card is not body text, and at 400 it read visibly thin beside the same figure on Lightyear.
components.css: .ds-stat-card { font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background-color: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2dfda; border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px oklch(0.24 0.012 60 / 0.05); } .ds-stat-label { margin-bottom: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #69625b; } .ds-stat-value { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 1.3rem + 0.9vw, 1.875rem); font-weight: 550; line-height: 1.2; color: #241e1a; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: The one place brass marks location. A 0.125rem underline scales in from scaleX(0) over 300ms on hover and on active, so the indicator grows from the link rather than sliding along the bar. Active also goes bold and brass; hover previews the same indicator without the weight change.
components.html: SummaryInstruments
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; } .ds-nav-link { position: relative; display: block; padding: 0.5rem; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.65); text-decoration: none; transition: color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link.is-active { color: #8d621f; } .ds-nav-link.is-active { font-weight: bold; } .ds-nav-indicator { position: absolute; bottom: -0.125rem; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 0.125rem; background-color: #8d621f; transform: scaleX(0); transition: transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover .ds-nav-indicator, .ds-nav-link.is-active .ds-nav-indicator { transform: scaleX(1); }

components.name: Value Flash
components.description: The price-change pulse: a cell animates from transparent to gain-wash or loss-wash and back over 3s. It is the only animation in the system exempted from prefers-reduced-motion by name, because it carries information rather than decoration — the global reduce rule crushes every animation to 0.01ms and this one is explicitly restored to 3s.
components.css: @keyframes ds-pulse-increase { 0% { background-color: transparent; } 50% { background-color: #e6f5e9; } 100% { background-color: transparent; } } @keyframes ds-pulse-decrease { 0% { background-color: transparent; } 50% { background-color: #ffebe8; } 100% { background-color: transparent; } } .ds-flash-up { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #287b46; animation: ds-pulse-increase 3s ease-in-out; transition: background-color 3s ease-in-out; } .ds-flash-down { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #b33834; animation: ds-pulse-decrease 3s ease-in-out; transition: background-color 3s ease-in-out; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-flash-up, .ds-flash-down { animation-duration: 3s !important; } }

components.name: Toast
components.description: Fixed top-right at 350px, tinted by a single --toast-bg custom property that each variant reassigns. It teleports out of #app to body, which is exactly why the font stack is declared on body rather than on #app: move the declaration and the toast silently renders in a different typeface than the app behind it.
components.css: .ds-toast-container { position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; z-index: 1090; width: max-content; max-width: 100%; padding: 1rem; pointer-events: none; } .ds-toast { --toast-bg: #69625b; width: 350px; max-width: 100%; font-family: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; pointer-events: auto; color: #ffffff; background-color: var(--toast-bg); background-clip: padding-box; border-radius: 0.25rem; box-shadow: 0 0.5rem 1.5rem oklch(0.24 0.012 60 / 0.14); } .ds-toast.is-success { --toast-bg: #287b46; } .ds-toast.is-error { --toast-bg: #b33834; } .ds-toast.is-info { --toast-bg: #316ca5; } .ds-toast.is-warning { --toast-bg: #8d621f; } .ds-toast-body { padding: 0.75rem; word-wrap: break-word; }

narrative.northStar: The Statement. A private-bank statement, not a trading terminal. Warm archival paper, deep ink, one metal accent. Nothing glows; things are printed. The interface is a document you sit with, and the numbers are the only things on it that were ever meant to be read closely.
narrative.overview: The material is paper and ink. Grounds are warm at hue 85 — a barely-there ochre cast that keeps white cards from reading as clinical — and every ink is warm at hue 60, so nothing on screen is the blue-grey the previous world defaulted to. Structure comes from hairlines, not shadow: where an edge exists it is 1px and warm, and where elevation exists it is a tinted whisper derived from the ink itself, never from neutral black. Colour is scarce and spent on meaning. There is exactly one accent, brass, and it marks three things: where you are, what you are focused on, and what is currently filtering the data. Green and red mean gain and loss, at matched lightness so a loss cannot look louder than an equal gain. Everything else is ink on paper. Density is deliberately high and the type carries it: one face, weight 550 for headings rather than 600 or 700, and tabular-nums inherited from body so every money column aligns. This is an interface built for someone who already knows what every column means.
keyCharacteristics: Warm grounds at hue 85 and warm inks at hue 60; no neutral grey anywhere in the ramp
Hairline-bordered, near-flat surfaces; shadow only where something genuinely floats, and always tinted from ink
One accent — brass — for navigation, focus, and active filters. Nothing else
Gain and loss locked to the same lightness, so equal magnitudes carry equal weight
Every colour resolves to a token authored in OKLCH; components declare none, and the stylesheet layer holds raw hex in exactly one declaration
Tables on desktop become label/value cards under 768px — the signature responsive move
Native platform primitives over hand-rolled ones: <dialog> for modals, ::picker(select) for dropdowns

rules.name: Gain and loss are locked to L = 0.520
rules.body: Equal magnitudes carry equal visual weight. Neither may be re-toned independently, and neither may be lightened to "soften" a loss.

rules.name: Brass is the only brand accent
rules.body: Nav active state, focus ring, primary action, active filter chip. Nothing else. If a screen has two brass elements competing for primary, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: Gain and loss are reserved for signed monetary movement
rules.body: They never decorate and never indicate non-financial success or failure. The shipped code diverges at eight sites, all of them loss and all inherited: destructive intent (.dialog-btn.danger, .btn-danger, .action-btn.danger:hover, two .remove-btn:hover rules) and validation error (.is-invalid, .invalid-feedback, .total-value.invalid). The count grew from six, so the divergence is expanding rather than shrinking. Resolve it by moving those sites to a dedicated danger token, not by restating the rule more loosely.

rules.name: ink-faint is not body text
rules.body: At 3.65:1 it satisfies non-text contrast and AA large text only. Its sanctioned uses are chart axis ticks, disabled control glyphs, and decorative rules. Every piece of small text — labels, captions, the build hash, stat-card labels, table meta — uses ink-soft at 6.02:1. This rule is what prevents the old gray-500 mistake recurring under a new name.

rules.name: State layers use color-mix() against the base token
rules.body: Hover and active states are never a second hardcoded colour. Declared and gated: today there is exactly one consumer and it is not a state layer — the summary chart loading veil at color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface) 72%, transparent). Every hover still resolves to a second token. The veil is nonetheless the precedent to copy: mix against a token, never against a literal.

rules.name: No component declares a colour
rules.body: Every value resolves to a token in the @theme static block of ui/styles/theme.css. That block is the only palette; a second one is a fork, not a shortcut.

rules.name: One face, and headings are weight 550
rules.body: Geist Variable is declared once on body and everything inherits it. h1–h6 share font-weight 550, line-height 1.2, and text-wrap: balance. 550 is not a rounding artefact of 500 — it is Lightyear heading weight to the number, reachable only because Geist wght axis is continuous, and it is the half step that keeps a heading distinct from the 600 label gesture beneath it. Geist Mono is the single sanctioned exception and is confined to the Monaco config editor.

rules.name: Every figure is tabular-nums
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set once on body and inherits everywhere. A component that introduces its own font-variant-numeric, or a font stack without tabular figures, breaks the alignment of every right-aligned money column beneath it and makes digits jitter during the price flash.

rules.name: The label gesture is uppercase, 600, 0.05em
rules.body: Two rules are the gesture: table headers at 0.75rem in brass-deep, mobile card labels at 0.8125rem in gray-700. Twelve uppercase label rules are live in total, so ten are variants across five distinct specs — including three sites at 0.5px tracking, which at 0.75rem is 0.0417em, not 0.05em. Normalizing them is a phased task with a visual-baseline cost; until then, do not cite "the label gesture" as if the code speaks with one voice.

rules.name: Reach for a hairline before a shadow
rules.body: If two surfaces need separating, that is a border. Shadow is reserved for the four things that genuinely float: the dropdown, the select picker, the toast, and the sticky nav.

rules.name: Two naming systems, one palette
rules.body: signal-indigo holds the brass value, control-graphite holds ink-soft, status-* hold the semantic signals, and the gray-* ramp holds warm neutrals. Neither naming system is a fork — a fork is two sources of truth; this is one source with two sets of names pointing into it. New work uses the semantic names; existing code keeps its legacy name until its component is migrated. signal-indigo still has sixteen references across ten files.

rules.name: Scoped styles are injected unlayered
rules.body: A <style scoped> block in a Vue component beats every @layer, including components. That is why an override "works" and why it is invisible to anyone reading the cascade. Never use one to override a components.css rule and expect the layer order to explain it.

dos: Reach for a 1px hairline before a shadow. If two surfaces need separating, that is a border.
Spend brass only on navigation state, focus rings, the primary action, and the active filter chip.
Add every new token to the @theme static block in ui/styles/theme.css, authored in OKLCH, and consume it as var(--color-*) or its Tailwind utility.
Keep gain and loss at L = 0.520, so an equal loss cannot look louder than a gain.
Use ink-soft for small text. ink-faint is for axis ticks, disabled glyphs, and rules.
Set the uppercase 0.75rem / 600 / 0.05em label for every column header and field label.
Let font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums inherit from body. Every money column depends on it.
Ship both renderings when adding a data column: the desktop table cell and the mobile card pair.
Hold the page shell at mx-auto mt-4 w-full max-w-app px-3. The gutter is intentional.
Reuse .platform-btn when a new surface needs a selected-one-of-many row. The summary chart time-range filter does exactly that and adds no CSS; a fifth resting treatment is what would be wrong.
State a chart values as text in its legend. The colours are an index into the legend, not the data.

Add a new route to ui/tests/visual/palette.spec.ts when you build one. It walks every visible text node for AA and the first fifteen tab stops for the focus ring, on three viewports, against stubbed data — and it catches what the screenshot comparator structurally cannot, a colour that moved but stayed close.
donts: Write a hex literal in a component or a stylesheet. There is exactly one in theme.css and four declarations of three distinct values in index.html, and every one has a recorded reason. A near-miss hex is a fork, and the pixel gate cannot police it: the comparator runs at maxDiffPixels: 0 but leaves Playwright per-pixel threshold at its default, so a colour that is merely close passes silently.
Treat --color-signal-indigo as a second accent. It is brass under an old name and it is leaving.

Use gain or loss for anything other than the sign of a value. No green "active" chips, no red "new" badges. The eight inherited danger and validation uses of loss are a known divergence, not a licence to add more — and the count has already grown once.
Introduce a second text face. One is declared, on body, and everything inherits it. The serif was built and removed; rebuilding it needs a rendered screenshot, not a rationale.

Add a radius value. Controls are 0.25rem, containers are 0.5rem. A container inside a container does not get a smaller radius — it gets a hairline. The one surviving 0.375rem radius is debt, not precedent.
Put a background fill back on .table thead th. It was removed because it collided with the active filter chips, which are the brass-wash element on a data surface.

Describe the legend swatch stroke as an accessibility feature. It is a 1.56:1 seam; the legend text is what satisfies non-text contrast. The donut arcs carry no stroke at all — the gap and the palette 3:1 floor already do that job.

Build a custom listbox, popover, or modal. <select> is styled through ::picker(select) and the dialogs are native <dialog>; both give you the top layer, the keyboard model, and scroll containment for free. A hand-rolled replacement has to reimplement all three and will get one of them wrong.
Animate anything that is not confirming a state change. The value flash, the spinners, and the select picker 150ms open are the whole motion budget.
Put a <style scoped> block in a component to override a components.css rule and expect the layer order to explain it. Scoped styles are injected unlayered and therefore beat every @layer.
Reach for a gray-* value when a semantic token names the same role. The ramp exists for the component layer older internals, not for new work.

Cite ui/styles/components.css with a line number. It is a nine-line barrel of @imports; the rules live in ui/styles/components/ across buttons, surfaces, forms, modals, feedback, navigation, controls, mobile-cards, and motion.
